config.title: Merchant Settings
config.isMerchantTooltip: Players can double-click this token to open its shop.
config.shopNameHint: Blank names the shop after whoever runs it.
config.kindHint: Flavour only. Shown above the name in the shop.
config.descriptionHint: Shown to players. Links and inline rolls work.
config.descriptionPlaceholder: A cramped shop that smells of oil and iron filings.
config.tillTooltip: Everything in the till, converted to the coins prices are quoted in
config.tillHint: What this shop can pay out when the party sells to it.
config.hiddenTooltip: Players are never sent this inventory
config.openInventoryTooltip: Open this inventory to stock it
config.productsTooltip: How many different things this inventory carries. A roll table fills it back up to this number.
config.productsLabel: How many different products this inventory carries
config.maxStackLabel: Maximum quantity of any one item
config.depthSummary: Type, rarity, and price each limit how many copies of an item can be stocked. The lowest applicable limit determines the quantity. A setting of 0 means no limit.
config.depthWorldNote: These limits come from Merchant’s world settings. This inventory’s Depth setting scales them up or down.
config.purchasedNote: Items bought from this inventory are removed and never restocked. Its stock is whatever the party has sold to the shop.
config.drawLabel: How many items to draw from this table
config.removeTableTooltip: Take this table off the inventory
config.noInventories: No inventories yet. Add one to start stocking this merchant.
config.overriding: Currently overriding the schedule. The next opening or closing hour will set it straight.
config.tillEmpty: An empty till cannot buy anything — the party will be refused when they try to sell.
config.globalMarkupHint: The baseline for everything in this shop. Each inventory multiplies against it.
config.pricingNone: No price until one is agreed with the party on the slate.
config.maxStackTooltipInfinite: The most of any one item a table roll will leave here. This inventory never runs out, so nothing else is capped by it.
config.maxStackTooltipFinite: The most of any one item this inventory will hold — a table roll, and a quantity you type in the shop window.
config.tableAuto: Drawn again every time this inventory restocks.
config.tableManual: Drawn only when you press Restock.
config.restockEverythingTooltip: Bring every inventory back to its quantities and roll all of its tables
config.drawTooltip: How many items to take from this table. {when}
config.queryNote: Items are pulled directly from the currently installed compendiums, so the available content stays current automatically.
config.queryUnavailable: Stocking from the compendiums needs a newer Coffee Pub Blacksmith. Until then this shelf draws from its roll tables.
config.manualNote: Nothing is drawn in. Whatever you put on this shelf is all it carries, and a restock tops those rows back up to their quantity without adding anything you did not choose.
config.addInventoryHint: Add a container to this merchant — a shelf, a back room, a case of curios.
config.depthTooltip: How deep this shelf stacks a thing it carries — one lantern or eight. Scales the world limits below; Products is how many different things it carries, and Max stack is the ceiling on any one of them.
config.portraitTooltip: Click to change the portrait. The token art changes with it.
config.illustrationHint: A picture of the place itself, shown behind the shop card, and a tint washed over it. Clear either to remove it.
config.tint: Shop tint — a colour for this shop’s card
config.curatedTooltip: Draw from the compendiums configured in Blacksmith — the ones this world officially uses
config.customTooltip: Draw only from compendiums you drop here, whether or not they are curated
config.curatedHint: Drawn from the item compendiums configured in Blacksmith: {list}.
config.dropCompendium: Drop a compendium here to draw from it
config.removeSourceTooltip: Take this compendium off the list
config.sourceMissingTooltip: This compendium is no longer installed. Nothing is drawn from it.
config.sourceUncuratedTooltip: Not in Blacksmith’s curated set. Blacksmith does not yet draw from an uncurated pack, so this one is listed but not stocked from — add it to Blacksmith’s item compendiums to use it today.
config.curatedHintNone: Blacksmith has no item compendiums configured, so this shelf has nothing to draw from. Configure them there, or switch to a list of this shelf’s own.
config.dropTable: Drop a roll table here to stock this inventory by rolling
config.drawNote: Existing items are restocked first. Draws then add new items the merchant doesn’t already carry.

market.blurb: What goods are worth on {scene}, whoever is asking. Every merchant here prices against it, and it applies to what they pay as well as what they charge — which is what makes running goods between two places worth doing.

notify.notARollTable: Drop a roll table here, not a {what}.

notify.brokenTableRows: {count} result(s) from {tables} no longer exist and were skipped. The table points at content that has been renamed, moved or uninstalled.
notify.queryUnavailable: This inventory stocks from the compendiums, which needs a newer Coffee Pub Blacksmith.
notify.queryEmpty: Nothing installed matches what {inventory} asks for. Widen its kinds, rarities or price range.
notify.nothingToMerge: Nothing on that inventory is duplicated.
notify.compendiumNotAdded: That is not a compendium, or it is already on the list.
notify.compendiumAddFailed: Could not change this shelf’s compendiums.

notify.dropCompendiumHere: That is a compendium — drop it on the Compendiums list below.
notify.compendiumNeedsManual: This shelf draws from Blacksmith’s curated compendiums. Switch it to Manually Selected Compendiums to name your own.
notify.notAnItemPack: That compendium does not hold items, so a shelf cannot stock from it.
notify.dropTableOnTables: That is a roll table — drop it on the Roll tables list above.
notify.filteredTableRows: {count} rolled item(s) were outside what {inventory} carries and were left out.

settings.soundSlateAddHint: Played when something is put on the slate, to buy or to sell.
settings.soundSlateUpdateHint: Played when a quantity or a price on the slate is changed.
settings.soundSlateClearHint: Played when a line is taken off the slate, or the whole slate is wiped.
settings.soundTransactionHint: Played when goods and coin change hands.
settings.soundRestockHint: Played to the GM when an inventory or a whole shop finishes restocking.
settings.soundErrorHint: Played when an action is refused or fails.
settings.stockCapTypeHint: The most of one {type} a shop stocks at once, before price and rarity are considered. 0 means no limit from the type.
settings.stockCapRarityHint: The most of one {rarity} item a shop stocks at once. 0 means no limit from the rarity.
settings.headingMerchantHint: Shops and merchants: a token marked as a merchant opens a shop window players can buy from and sell to. What a shop stocks, what it charges and when it is open are set on the merchant itself — these are the world-wide rules every shop plays by.
settings.headingStockDepthHint: How many of one thing a shop stocks at once. Type, rarity and price each set a ceiling and the lowest wins; an inventory’s own Depth setting scales these up or down. 0 means that rule sets no limit.
settings.headingStockByTypeHint: How much of a kind of thing a shop keeps. A general store has rope by the coil and one crossbow.
settings.headingStockByRarityHint: The lever price cannot pull: two blades at the same price are not the same question if one of them is legendary.
settings.headingSoundHint: What a shop sounds like. Chosen by the GM for the table, but played only on the client that did the thing — nobody else hears you drop a rope onto your slate. Silent by default.

rate.farmWarning: Above {safe}% this inventory pays more than it charges, so the shop can be sold to and bought from at a profit. Offers are capped instead, and a party the town likes is paid less than a neutral one. Raise Sell, or lower this.
rate.purchaseHint: What the shop pays the party for their goods.
rate.sellHint: What it then charges for them, on top of the Global Markup.
rate.markupHint: Multiplied against the shop's Global Markup.

reputation.good: You are thought well of here, so this shop treats you better — on what you buy and on what it pays you.
reputation.bad: You are poorly thought of here, so this shop charges you more and pays you less.
